clue.text: Club's court date

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A club announces the date of its court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a golf club with a broad head, traditionally made of timber, used for long shots.

clue.text: Office item used to be involved in bet

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or intricate, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
these five letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some office gadget has been caught up in a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to be' supplies letters here, not a link; 'involved' reads like 'mixed up in a bet' but jumbles the words in bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste bin is the basket under every office desk for rubbish, so it is a typical office fixture.

clue.text: Vegetable garden's boundary land

parts.note: a swede is a root vegetable, called rutabaga in the US

indicators.note: a boundary is the edge of something, here the closing edge of the word

parts.note: the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A vegetable patch sits at the edge of a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: A swede is the root vegetable Americans call a rutabaga.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian country, and land is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: '1812', for one, is bound to have noisy climax and corny bit

parts.note: to bound is to leap

indicators.note: a climax comes at the end, so take the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of noisy
an ear is the part of a corn plant that bears the grain

explanation.surface: Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture, with its cannon-fire finale and sentimental passages, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make '1812' look like the overture, which really does have a noisy climax; it is just the year, divisible by four.
explanation.definitionFit: 1812 is divisible by four and not a century year, so it had a 29th of February: it is an example of the type.

clue.text: It has a canopy of raised support

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word of turned upside down
a rest is a support, as in an armrest

explanation.surface: Something sports an awning held on a lifted prop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canopy' suggests a bed or tent, but it is the upper layer of leaves in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopy is the ceiling of leaves formed by tree crowns, which is a characteristic layer of woodland.

clue.text: Former actor producing 'Female Resistance'

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An actor of the past puts on a play called Female Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Antony Sher was a celebrated Royal Shakespeare Company actor who died in 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony Sher, a leading British stage actor, died in 2021, so he is a past performer.

clue.text: Victoria's one abysmally low year?

indicators.note: abysmally means very badly, so the letters that follow are badly arranged

parts.note: all seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria had a dreadful year of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria's famous 'We are not amused' is the classic example of a monarch speaking of herself as we.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's use of we for I is called the royal we, and Victoria is the best-known user.

clue.text: Country hotel's playing ball

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about in play, so they rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rural hotel is hosting a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hotel' reads as one phrase, but Country is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Censor's current turnover

indicators.note: a turnover flips something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: A censor's present output of work is under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current turnover' looks like a figure for business income; current is the sea movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to cut or alter text, which is what a censor does to material.

clue.text: Insult by a President at Conference? Make yourself scarce!

parts.note: to dis is slang for to insult
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for president
Conference is a popular British variety of pear

explanation.surface: Someone tells a delegate who insulted the President at a conference to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety, not a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To make yourself scarce is to go away, so the command matches an imperative to vanish.

clue.text: Position sack and turn over light

indicators.note: and simply adds the next piece on after the previous ones

parts.note: to set something is to position it
to sack an employee is to fire them
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a bag and flips a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: No word marks the initials of turn over; the solver must spot that the letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to ignite it, which is to cause it to burn.

clue.text: Bird pen fixture with round ridge opening tipped over

indicators.note: something tipped over ends up the other way round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: the nib is the writing point fixed on a pen
the round letter O

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so take the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of ridge

explanation.surface: A fitting for a bird enclosure, with a rounded crest, has fallen over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests a bird enclosure, but it is the writing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar small songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Polish river comes first as major river

indicators.note: this says one piece is placed ahead of the other rather than after it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
to hone is to sharpen or polish

explanation.surface: A river in Poland is ranked ahead of a bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish loses its capital letter's meaning: it is the verb, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is one of Europe's great waterways, flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Fun is editing leader for paper

parts.note: a treat is something enjoyable
taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so take the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of editing

explanation.surface: A journalist enjoys editing the lead article for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'editing leader' sounds like writing an editorial; leader just takes an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper can mean a scholarly essay, and a treatise is a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: What you aim to do, only without Victor

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Your goal is the same, just minus a man called Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking; here it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver's aim is to work out the clue, so the definition addresses you directly about this very puzzle.

clue.text: Jack Ball at Houston bankers' convenience

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
a ball is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two sides, so take the outside letters of the word

parts.note: the two outside letters of Houston

explanation.surface: A man named Jack goes to a dance in Houston provided for bank staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A convenience is a British euphemism for a public toilet; john is American slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: John is US slang for a lavatory, and a public convenience is a British name for one.

clue.text: Brother's kitchen item reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a fryer is a pan or appliance for frying

explanation.surface: A sibling's cooking utensil is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Brother is the title of a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Stories of old people taking on new role

indicators.note: new suggests the word is made over into a fresh form, so its letters rearrange

parts.note: folk are people
these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly people are given a fresh part to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old people' reads as a phrase, but the split is after 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore is the traditional tales and beliefs of a community handed down through generations.

clue.text: With Dicky, one could be left in it

definitions.text: one could be left in it

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky might be abandoned along with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a man's name, but it is the British slang for poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is left money or property in a testament, the document that names who inherits.

clue.text: Gale's hiding book, a dictionary

indicators.note: hiding means concealing something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a wester is a westerly gale, here with its possessive
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A woman called Gale has a book tucked away, which happens to be a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Gale reads as a name, but it is the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Webster's is the American English dictionary founded by Noah Webster, so it is one example of the kind.

clue.text: Touchdown, in two words, makes you experience sadness

parts.note: to touch is to feel
down means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: An aircraft landing, or a rugby try, makes someone miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'Touchdown' itself into its two parts, as 'in two words' admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is an idiom for low spirits, so to feel blue is to experience unhappiness.

clue.text: Small US state capital — not Hudson?

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the part named next

parts.note: the capital of Arkansas
Rock Hudson was the Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A small American state capital apparently is not on the Hudson river.
explanation.walkthrough: Hudson suggests the river of New York, but it is the actor Rock Hudson whose first name goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Little is a straightforward synonym of small in size.

clue.text: Sun bear: unstable potential killer

indicators.note: something unstable will not stay as it is, so the letters move about

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun
these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sun bear is a volatile animal that could kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun bear is a real Asian species, so the clue reads as a wildlife warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy curved cavalry sword, a weapon that can kill.

clue.text: Obnoxious type of quiet Scottish island

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Muck is a small island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person comes from a silent Highland isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shmuck is Yiddish-derived slang for a contemptible or foolish person.

clue.text: A smashing time here for a rock star?

definitions.text: A smashing time here for a rock star?

parts.note: surface reading: a place for a wonderful time
setter's reading: the place where a wild musician literally smashes things up on tour

explanation.walkthrough: Smashing is British for excellent, but rock stars are notorious for wrecking the lodgings they stay in.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashing the room where they stay overnight is a cliché of rock bands on tour.

clue.text: Criminal carrier has nothing to hide

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
nothing is zero, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A criminal courier has nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal carrier' reads as a drug mule, but Criminal stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster or thug.

clue.text: A dive's possible feature food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a diving position with knees pulled to the chest
second meaning: British school slang for snacks and sweets

explanation.walkthrough: A dive suggests a seedy bar serving food, but it is a plunge into a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers perform tucked somersaults, and tuck is informal British slang for food, especially at boarding school.

clue.text: Company was boastful

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a team of people working together, as on a ship
second meaning: an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working group, and crew is an older past tense of crow, meaning bragged.

clue.text: Cast is turning fat — a hindrance when on the road

definitions.text: a hindrance when on the road

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw or cast
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: An acting company is gaining weight, which is a problem when touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors, but it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short post set in a road to stop vehicles, so it obstructs traffic.

clue.text: Potential big name actor going around college: time to go red

going around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a starlet is a young actress tipped for fame

T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rising actor at university reaches the moment to blush.
explanation.walkthrough: The T removed is the first one in the starlet; C then fills its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red.
